children: The market has real concerns about the French fiscal situation, says Domini Impact Investments' Maria Llerena, as 10-year OAT yields rose above 5% for the first time in 24 years this week. With bond yields at or around 5%, French debt is now trading at yields above those of Italy and Greece, the director of financial research says. "Debt to GDP is close to 120% and the country has been running deficits above 5% for four straight years," she says, adding that protests, a government trying to pass a budget and presidential elections in the spring of 2027 "complicate things further." (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
